changes: Adds Rollout Story 1 of the Story-relevance dynamic validation tiers plan. New core/validation-command-identity.ts gives every configured validation command a stable id: a declared id is kept verbatim, an undeclared one gets a deterministic prov- id over the narrow portable tuple of command, args, repo-relative cwd and shell, and a commandSetDigest covers the normalized inventory including label and focus. The same module owns the canonical legacy pin resolver (exact commandId, legacy-exact normalized tuple, pinned_command_missing, pinned_command_ambiguous, pinned_command_non_inventory). New core/validation-relevance-input.ts collects a normalized StoryRelevanceInput through the existing shared rename-aware and freshness readers rather than re-deriving them. New core/validation-tier-planner.ts defines the three tier names, the subset invariant and the fail-closed widening matrix, where every reason code carries a plain-language gloss declared in the same table. New handlers/validation-plan.ts exposes it as a read-only CLI. verifier.ts and validation-evidence-reuse.ts had their existing command normalization and legacy string parse EXTRACTED and exported so identity and pin resolution reuse one owner instead of duplicating the rules; buildRoutineValidationIdentity behaviour is unchanged. proof-or-stop.config.json registers the new suite as validate command 121.
usage: node packages/main/dist/cli.js validation_plan --storyId=B-xxxx --tier=fast|intermediate|full [--explain] [--json]. It prints requestedTier, effectiveTier, a runtime-derived selected-of-total count, per-command inclusion reasons, unclassified inputs, each escalation reason code followed by a plain-language gloss, an estimated duration with its basis, and finalAuthority: no. It executes no validation command, writes no evidence and changes no gate.
expectedOutcome: An operator runs validation_plan against a Story and sees the full command inventory with stable ids, whether each recorded evidence pin resolves, which Story inputs were collected, and a readable explanation of why the effective tier is still the whole repository rather than a reduced set. Validation does not get faster: this increment can never shrink a set, by design.
actualTranscript: node packages/main/dist/cli.js validation_plan --storyId=B-a745 --tier=fast prints: status: plan / requestedTier: story-fast (requested as "fast") / effectiveTier: repository-full / sourceKind: configured / selected: 121 of 121 validation unit(s) / reductionApplied: false / finalAuthority: no, followed by four escalation reasons each with a gloss (impact_index_unusable, command_exclusion_unproven, unclassified_material_input, pinned_command_non_inventory), per-unit inclusion reasons, unclassified inputs, an estimatedDuration line naming its basis, and an inventoryWarning naming the runtime count of commands still on provisional ids. Missing storyId is rejected with 'validation_plan: storyId is required'; --tier=quick with 'unknown tier "quick" (expected one of fast, intermediate, full)'.
outcomeDiff: No difference in the delivered surface. One acceptance criterion changed under review rather than being met as written: CHK-002:edge:0 asserted that an unresolvable legacy pin stops with pinned_command_missing, and finding F-001 deliberately reversed that so a legacy string matching nothing is classified pinned_command_non_inventory and widens instead of stopping. That intent carries a permanent supersession waiver naming the two committed fixtures that cover the replacement behaviour. The old behaviour made the command self-referentially unusable and would have stopped on essentially every real story.
limitations: This increment performs NO relevance pruning and never returns a reduced tier; effectiveTier is a TypeScript literal type, not a union, so no pruning code path can exist. Validation therefore does not get faster - the value here is stable identity, honest pin resolution and an explain output. Impact index, exclusion proofs, worktree overlay, runner decomposition, signed selection artifacts, tier execution and the kill switch all belong to Rollout Stories 2 to 4 and are explicitly excluded. One receipt is knowingly weak: CHK-005:happy:0 is pinned to the selector 'finalAuthority: no', which prints on every branch including failures and produced a documented false positive (F-002); verification pins are immutable so it could not be corrected, and the discrimination is instead proven by a committed fixture. On whether an unresolvable LEGACY pin should stop, the governing spec's widening matrix qualifies the stop with 'explicit' while its resolver step 4 and Step 7 invariant do not, and this story's own frozen CHK-002:edge:0 encodes the unqualified reading; the implementation follows the qualified reading because under the unqualified one the planner is self-referentially unusable (its own acceptance evidence pins the planner command) and nothing is pruned either way. An independent Codex host filed that choice as a defect; the reconciliation is delegated to the document owner via the committed repository draft docs/story/drafts/reconcile-pin-resolution-rules-tiers-plan.
pitfalls: Four things cost real time and the next person should know them. (1) The global proof-or-stop binary resolves into ANOTHER story's worktree (.worktrees/B-fe8f) and is a pre-rename build, so it fails with 'promptEnvelope.roles contains unknown role'; dispatch and agent_prompt are both dead through it. Every command in this story had to run as node packages/main/dist/cli.js. Diagnose the entrypoint before believing an 'unknown role' error is a registry defect - it is not. (2) The proof selector on a mechanical receipt must DISCRIMINATE. 'finalAuthority: no' prints on every branch, so the receipt recorded pass while its own outputTail showed status: stop. Pins are immutable, so a bad selector is uncorrectable - choose it as carefully as the command. (3) Registering one new CLI command needs six registries, not one: registry.ts, command-catalog.ts, command-policy.ts, config.ts DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS, cli/activity-policy.ts READ_ONLY_COMMANDS and process-fact-levels.ts, each failing closed. And a new test suite needs THREE inventories - npm script, test:serial-reference and RESOURCE_POLICY - plus validate.commands if any evidence will pin it, which is what F-005 was. (4) Do not copy a count out of a subagent report into a durable record without re-running the query; that produced two findings here, the second inside the correction for the first. (5) A claim such as 'filed for the spec owner' must name an in-repository artifact that exists at write time; a session task chip is not one, and gap_log is currently broken, so story_draft is the durable deferral mechanism.
